record.original_question: For incompressible fluid dynamics, especially at very large Reynolds number where viscosity is very small, is violent turbulence fundamentally caused by rough dependence on initial data rather than ordinary sensitive dependence on initial data? In this setting, rough dependence means that arbitrarily small perturbations of the initial condition can become substantial essentially instantly; for the Euler equations, at any nonzero time the solution map from initial data to the solution is continuous but nowhere locally uniformly continuous and nowhere differentiable. Does this mechanism, or the very large derivative of the Navier-Stokes solution map in the high-Reynolds-number regime, explain why sufficiently large-Reynolds-number turbulence develops violently in short time?

evidence.quote: My conjecture is that the high Reynolds number violent turbulence is due to such rough dependence on initial data, rather than sensitive dependence on initial data of chaos.

In summary, not large enough Reynolds number turbulence may be due to sensitive dependence on initial data of chaos, while large enough Reynolds number turbulence may be due to rough dependence on initial data.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider incompressible fluid dynamics on a smooth bounded (or periodic) spatial domain. The Navier–Stokes equations read
  ∂_t u + (u·∇)u = −∇p + ν Δu,  ∇·u = 0,
with prescribed initial data u(0)=u_0 in a suitable Sobolev space, where ν>0 is the kinematic viscosity and the Reynolds number is Re ~ 1/ν. The Euler equations correspond to ν=0:
  ∂_t u + (u·∇)u = −∇p,  ∇·u = 0.

Define the solution map S_t : u_0 ↦ u(t,·). For the Euler equations it is known that, for any t ≠ 0, S_t is continuous on the relevant Sobolev space but is nowhere locally uniformly continuous and nowhere Fréchet differentiable; equivalently, arbitrarily small perturbations of the initial condition can produce order-one changes in the solution after arbitrarily short time ("rough dependence on initial data"). For the Navier–Stokes equations with ν>0 the solution map is differentiable, but the operator norm of its Fréchet derivative admits an upper bound that grows like exp(C√(t·Re) + C_1 t).

Question. Is it true that, in the high-Reynolds-number regime, violent fully developed turbulence is fundamentally caused by this "rough dependence on initial data" mechanism (rather than the standard "sensitive dependence on initial data" of finite-dimensional chaos)? More precisely, does the norm of the Fréchet derivative of the Navier–Stokes solution map S_t (at fixed t>0) tend to infinity as Re → ∞, and does this divergence quantitatively account for the short-time onset of violent turbulent behavior at sufficiently large Reynolds number, while moderate-Reynolds-number turbulence is instead governed by ordinary chaotic sensitive dependence?
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture remains open. Subsequent work has provided supporting analytical bounds (an exp(C√(t Re)+C_1 t) bound on the norm of the Navier–Stokes solution-map derivative) and numerical evidence of short-term unpredictability at high Reynolds number under periodic boundary conditions, but no proof that the derivative norm diverges as Re→∞ or a rigorous derivation that violent turbulence is caused by rough dependence has been established.

status_evidence.title: Distinction of turbulence from chaos – rough dependence on initial data
status_evidence.snippet: Conjectures that high-Reynolds-number violent turbulence is due to rough dependence on initial data rather than sensitive dependence; provides bound exp(C√(tRe)+C_1 t).
status_evidence.claim: Conjecture stated and partial bounds proved; full conjecture not resolved.

status_evidence.title: Short term unpredictability of high Reynolds number turbulence
status_evidence.snippet: Numerical investigations support short-term unpredictability of high-Reynolds-number flows consistent with the rough-dependence theory.
status_evidence.claim: Provides numerical support but not a proof.

status_evidence.title: Major open problems in chaos theory, turbulence and PDEs
status_evidence.snippet: Lists rough dependence vs. sensitive dependence as a major open problem in turbulence theory.
